lesson.text: Remember? Which one is alive: a rabbit or a rock? The rabbit, of course! But how can a scientist tell for sure? Today we learn the signs of life.
Every living thing does all of these. It feeds: it eats, or makes its own food. It breathes: it uses air. It grows. It reproduces: it makes young or seeds. And it responds to what happens around it.
Plants are alive too, even though they stay in one place. A sunflower makes its own food from sunlight, grows tall, makes seeds and turns its leaves towards the light.
Some things were once living but are not alive now: a wooden plank came from a tree, and a dry leaf fell from one. Other things were never alive: a rock, a cloud, a metal key.
Careful! A fire grows and a robot moves, but they are not alive: they do not feed, grow and reproduce like a living thing. To be living, a thing must do all of the signs of life.
Scientists sort living things into big groups. Plants make their own food from sunlight. Animals eat other living things. Fungi, like mushrooms and moulds, feed on dead and rotting things.
Bacteria are living things so tiny that you need a microscope to see them. Some make people ill, but many help: some turn milk into yoghurt, and some in your tummy help you digest your food.
Try it in the world: in a meadow in your world, find three living things, three once-living things (a plank, a dry leaf) and three never-living things. Next: sorting with keys.

exercises.prompt: Which one is a living thing?
exercises.hint: Which one feeds and grows?
exercises.explain: A mushroom is a fungus: it feeds, grows and makes new mushrooms. The others are not alive.

exercises.prompt: A tree is a living thing.
exercises.hint: Does a tree grow and make seeds?
exercises.explain: Yes: a tree feeds, grows, makes seeds and responds to light, so it is alive.

exercises.prompt: What do all living things do?
exercises.hint: Think of a plant and an animal. What do they both do?
exercises.explain: Every living thing grows. Plants cannot run, fly or talk, but they grow.

exercises.prompt: A rock grows bigger by eating.
exercises.hint: Does a rock feed?
exercises.explain: False: a rock does not feed, grow or reproduce. It was never alive.

exercises.prompt: Which group makes its own food from sunlight?
exercises.hint: Which group has green leaves?
exercises.explain: Plants use sunlight to make their own food in their leaves.

exercises.prompt: Which of these was once living?
exercises.hint: Which one came from a tree?
exercises.explain: A wooden plank came from a tree, so it was once living. Glass, metal and stone were never alive.

exercises.prompt: The mould on old bread is a...
exercises.hint: Which group feeds on dead and rotting things?
exercises.explain: Mould is a fungus: it feeds on the old bread.

exercises.prompt: A fire grows and uses air, so it is a living thing.
exercises.hint: Does a fire do all the signs of life?
exercises.explain: False: a fire does not feed, grow and reproduce like a living thing. It is not alive.

exercises.prompt: Which one shows a living thing responding?
exercises.hint: Which one reacts to something it senses?
choices: A cat jumps when it hears a bang
A ball rolls down a hill
A kite rises in the wind
exercises.explain: The cat hears the bang and reacts by jumping: that is responding, a sign of life.

exercises.prompt: What do fungi feed on?
exercises.hint: Think of mushrooms on an old log.
exercises.explain: Fungi feed on dead and rotting things, like fallen logs and old bread.

exercises.prompt: Why are bacteria hard to spot?
exercises.hint: How big are bacteria?
choices: They are too small to see without a microscope
They only come out at night
exercises.explain: Bacteria are so tiny that you need a microscope to see them.

exercises.prompt: All bacteria make people ill.
exercises.hint: Think about milk and yoghurt.
exercises.explain: False: some bacteria make people ill, but many help, like the ones that turn milk into yoghurt.

exercises.prompt: Pip's robot moves, uses power and beeps when touched. Why is it not alive?
exercises.hint: Check every sign of life. Which ones can it not do?
choices: It cannot grow or reproduce by itself
It is made of shiny metal
exercises.explain: A robot does not feed, grow or make young robots by itself, so it is not a living thing.

exercises.prompt: A mushroom is a kind of plant.
exercises.hint: Can a mushroom make food from sunlight?
exercises.explain: False: a mushroom is a fungus. It cannot make food from sunlight; it feeds on dead and rotting things.

exercises.prompt: A seed looks still and dry. Is it living?
exercises.hint: What happens when you plant a seed and water it?
choices: Yes: give it water and it grows
exercises.explain: A seed is alive, only resting. With water and warmth it sprouts and grows into a plant.

exercises.prompt: Sort them: living or never living?
exercises.hint: Does it feed, grow and make young?
exercises.explain: Living: a rabbit, a sunflower. Never living: a rock, a plastic cup.

exercises.prompt: Match each sign of life to what it means.
matches: reacts to what is around it
eats or makes its own food
exercises.hint: Think of a rabbit doing each one in a meadow.
exercises.explain: Feeds: eats or makes its own food. Grows: gets bigger. Reproduces: makes young or seeds. Responds: reacts to what is around it.

exercises.prompt: Sort them: living, once living, or never living?
exercises.hint: Is it alive now? If not, did it come from something that was alive?
exercises.explain: Living: a mushroom and a sunflower. Once living: the plank and the dry leaf came from trees. Never living: a metal key and a cloud.

exercises.prompt: Sort the living things into their groups.
exercises.hint: Ask how each one gets its food: from sunlight, by eating, or from dead and rotting things?
exercises.explain: Plants make food from sunlight: the sunflower and the oak. Animals eat: the rabbit and the fox. Fungi feed on dead and rotting things: the mushroom and the mould.

exercises.prompt: A dry seed is planted. Put the steps in order to show it is alive.
items: A root and a shoot grow.
The seed is planted in soil.
It is watered and kept warm.
exercises.hint: Start with the resting seed. What does it need before it can grow?
exercises.explain: Plant the seed, water it and keep it warm. A root and a shoot grow, and the grown plant makes new seeds. It grows and reproduces, so it was alive all along.

exercises.prompt: Check Pip's robot against the signs of life. Which can it do?
exercises.hint: Go through the signs one by one: feed, breathe, grow, reproduce, respond.
exercises.explain: The robot moves and beeps when touched, but it cannot feed, grow or make young robots by itself. A living thing does all the signs, so the robot is not alive.

exercises.prompt: Nell finds 4 rabbits, 3 rocks, 5 flowers, 2 planks and 1 mushroom. How many living things did she find?
exercises.hint: Pick out only the things that are alive now, then add them up.
exercises.explain: Living: 4 rabbits, 5 flowers and 1 mushroom, and 4 + 5 + 1 = 10. Rocks were never alive, and planks are only once living.
